units.title: Making a Doctor's Appointment
units.script:
Man: Good morning. I'd like to make an appointment with the doctor.
Woman: Certainly. What day would you like to come?
Man: Is the doctor available tomorrow morning?
Woman: Let me check. Yes, there is an available appointment at ten thirty.
Man: That sounds good. How long do I need to wait?
Woman: Usually, you only need to wait about fifteen minutes.
Man: Okay. I'll come tomorrow at ten thirty.
Woman: All right. May I have your name, please?
Man: My name is David Brown.
Narrator: Why does the man call the woman?

units.title: Planning a Weekend Trip
units.script:
Woman: Do you have any plans for the weekend?
Man: Not yet. Why?
Woman: I'm thinking about going to the beach on Saturday. Would you like to come with me?
Man: That sounds interesting. How will we get there?
Woman: We can take the bus. It takes about two hours to reach the beach.
Man: What time should we leave?
Woman: I think we should leave at seven in the morning.
Man: Okay. Should I bring anything?
Woman: Bring some food, water, and your swimming clothes.
Man: Great! I'm looking forward to it.

parts.title: Part C — Talks
parts.directions: In Part C you will hear talks, such as a lecture or an announcement. After each talk you will answer several questions about it.

units.title: The Importance of Drinking Water
units.script:
Narrator: Listen to a talk about the importance of drinking water.
Woman: Good morning, everyone. Today, I would like to talk about the importance of drinking water. Water is very important for our bodies. It helps us stay healthy and gives our bodies the energy to do daily activities. Drinking enough water also helps us concentrate better when studying.Most people need about eight glasses of water every day, although the amount may vary depending on their activities and the weather. If we do not drink enough water, we may feel tired and have difficulty concentrating. Therefore, remember to drink water regularly, especially when the weather is hot.
Narrator: Question 36. What is the main topic of the talk?

questions.q: What is the main topic of the talk?
What may happen if people do not drink enough water?

units.title: The History of the Telephone
units.script:
Narrator: Listen to a talk about the history of the telephone.
Man: The telephone is one of the most important inventions in human history. It allows people to communicate with each other over long distances. Alexander Graham Bell is widely credited with inventing the first practical telephone in 1876. In the past, telephones were large and usually stayed in one place. People could only make calls using wires. Today, telephones have become smaller and more advanced. Smartphones allow people not only to make calls but also to send messages, take pictures, and access the internet. The telephone has changed the way people communicate in their daily lives.
Narrator: Who is widely credited with inventing the first practical telephone?

questions.q: When is the first practical telephone invented?
What can people do with modern smartphones besides making calls?
o: Send messages and access the internet.

units.title: The Benefits of Reading Books
units.script:
Narrator: Listen to a short lecture about reading books.
Woman: Reading books is a useful activity for students. It provides many benefits, especially for those who want to improve their language skills. First, reading helps students learn new vocabulary. When students read regularly, they become familiar with different words and expressions. Second, reading can improve writing skills. Students can learn how to organize sentences and develop ideas by reading different types of texts. Finally, reading also increases knowledge because books contain information about many subjects, such as science, history, and culture. For these reasons, students should make reading a regular habit.
Narrator: What is one benefit of reading books mentioned by the speaker?
Narrator: Who is probably the speaker?

What is one benefit of reading books mentioned by the speaker?

It reduces the need to study.

By encouraging students to write shorter texts only.
By making students read without understanding.

questions.q: What is not mentioned about the benefits of reading?
o: Students will familiar with different words and expressions.

Reading increases knowledge because books contain information about many subjects
Students should make regular reading habit.

units.title: Urban trees
units.passage:
Urban trees provide benefits that extend beyond their appearance. Their leaves provide shade, reducing the heat absorbed by streets and buildings. Trees also help manage rainwater: some water is intercepted by leaves, while roots improve the soil's ability to absorb rainfall.

However, planting trees in cities requires careful planning. A tree that grows well in a park may not be suitable for a narrow sidewalk where roots could damage pavement or underground pipes. Successful urban forestry therefore depends not simply on planting more trees, but on choosing appropriate species and caring for them over time.

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Why cities should remove old trees
The benefits of urban trees and the need for careful planning
Why all trees grow well on sidewalks

questions.q: The word "intercepted" in the passage is closest in meaning to
Why might a tree be unsuitable for a narrow sidewalk?
o: Its roots may damage pavement or pipes.
